title_en: Xi'an Municipal People's Procuratorate v. Wei Guoquan — theft case
ruling_gist_en: A motor vehicle is a item with special attributes, and its owner must assert ownership through a certificate of title. Transfer of ownership of a motor vehicle occurs only after the registration of transfer is completed. Meanwhile, the vehicle license plate registration system further strengthens the control of the owner or possessor over the vehicle. Therefore, even if the owner or possessor of a motor vehicle leaves the windows or lights on when leaving the vehicle, or leaves the keys in the vehicle, it cannot be determined that they have completely lost control over the vehicle, and thus the motor vehicle cannot be presumed to be a forgotten item. Under such circumstances, if a person, for the purpose of illegal possession, obtains the motor vehicle by secret theft, the act shall be convicted and punished as the crime of theft.

full_text_en:
Xi'an Municipal People's Procuratorate v. Wei Guoquan — theft case

【Ruling Summary】

A motor vehicle is property with special attributes, and the owner must assert ownership by means of a certificate of title. Transfer of ownership of a motor vehicle occurs only after the registration of the transfer has been completed. Meanwhile, the license plate registration system further enhances the control of the owner or possessor over the vehicle. Therefore, even if the owner or possessor of a motor vehicle leaves the vehicle with the windows and lights on and the key still in the ignition, it cannot be determined that they have completely lost control over the vehicle, and thus the vehicle cannot be presumed to be a mislaid item. Under such circumstances, if an actor, for the purpose of illegal possession, obtains the motor vehicle by stealth, the act shall be convicted and punished as theft.

Procuratorial Authority: Xi'an Municipal People's Procuratorate, Shaanxi Province.

Defendant: Wei Guoquan, male, 32 years old, Han ethnicity, residing in Wu Xing Jie Xiao Qu, Xi'an, taxi driver. Arrested on January 26, 2005.

The Xi'an Municipal People's Procuratorate, Shaanxi Province, initiated a public prosecution against the defendant Wei Guoquan for theft before the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court, Shaanxi Province.

The indictment alleged: In the early morning of April 10, 2004, Zheng Wei, an employee of Shaanxi Xinhua Xin Real Estate Co., Ltd., due to drunkenness, parked the company's white Lexus 400 sedan (license plate Shaan A-L5408, valued at RMB 373,380) on the motor vehicle lane opposite the Caesar Palace on Wenyi Road, Xi'an, with the keys left in the ignition and windows left open. At approximately 6:00 a.m. on the same day, the defendant Wei Guoquan (a taxi driver) passed by and noticed this situation. About an hour later, Wei Guoquan passed by the same section of road again and found the vehicle still parked in the same place. He then parked his taxi, surreptitiously entered the white Lexus, and noticing the keys were still in the ignition and no one was interfering, drove the car away and concealed it in the parking lot of the 323 Hospital of the People's Liberation Army on Jianshe West Road, Xi'an. Subsequently, Wei Guoquan used and squandered the mobile phone, leather shoes, and US dollars found in the car, and hid the golf clubs found therein at his sister's home. He also had the vehicle repaired and changed its license plates. In January 2005, the victim discovered the stolen vehicle, and the public security organs arrested the defendant Wei Guoquan. Wei Guoquan's conduct violated Article 264 of the Criminal Law of the PRC and constituted theft. The procuratorate requested a conviction and punishment according to law.

The procuratorial authority submitted the following evidence:

1. Statement of victim Zheng Wei. Main content: Zheng Wei was a driver for Shaanxi Xinhua Xin Real Estate Co., Ltd. At about 5:00 a.m. on April 10, 2004, due to drunkenness, he lost the company's white Lexus 400 sedan (license plate Shaan A-L5408) and later reported the loss.

2. Certificate of case resolution. Main content: On January 11, 2005, victim Zheng Wei reported to the First Brigade of the Comprehensive Division of the Criminal Investigation Bureau of Xi'an Public Security Bureau that he had found his missing vehicle in the parking lot of the Shaanxi Provincial Hospital. Public security officers arrested the driver Wei Guoquan the following evening. Upon inspection, the vehicle was confirmed to be the one lost by Zheng Wei.

3. Testimony of witness Wei Guoqi (brother of Wei Guoquan). Main content: The defendant Wei Guoquan drove a white Lexus sedan in April or May 2004 and told Wei Guoqi that the car belonged to a real estate developer. He said he found the car on Wenyi Road with its headlights on, windows open, and keys in the ignition, and wanted to drive it for fun, so he took it away and hid it. Wei Guoqi told Wei Guoquan to get rid of the car quickly, but Wei Guoquan said he would drive it for a few days and then discard it, but never did.

4. Vehicle registration information and testimony of witnesses Wang Lichun and Zheng Wei. Main content: The registered license plate number was Shaan A-L5408, the registered owner on the vehicle certificate was Wang Lichun, but the ownership of the vehicle belonged to Wang Liping.

5. Public security organ's seizure and inventory records, receipt slips, etc. Main content: Items seized from Wei Guoquan included the white Lexus 400 sedan, vehicle certificate, mobile phone, business cards, golf clubs, wallet, etc. The above items were retrieved by Zheng Wei.

6. Appraisal conclusion of items. Main content: The value of the Shaan A-L5408 white Lexus 400 sedan was RMB 373,380.

7. Seized vehicle repair invoices, used to prove that Wei Guoquan had the Lexus 400 sedan repaired and parts replaced.

8. Confession of defendant Wei Guoquan, who had no objection to the fact that he drove away the white Lexus 400 sedan involved in the case.

The defendant Wei Guoquan argued: The facts alleged in the indictment were generally correct, but some details were erroneous. He drove the car away to show off in front of friends, without the purpose of illegal possession. He had intended to return the car to its owner several times but failed to do so.

Wei Guoquan's defense counsel contended: 1. On the day of the incident, the vehicle involved was parked on a motor vehicle lane with windows open and keys left in the ignition, and the owner had lost control over the vehicle. Therefore, the vehicle was a mislaid item and not an object of theft; 2. Wei Guoquan did not take the car away by stealth, so his conduct did not satisfy the objective elements of theft; 3. Wei Guoquan did not alter the vehicle's characteristics or conceal it, and lacked subjective intent of illegal possession; 4. After the incident, Wei Guoquan compensated the victim for economic losses in the amount of RMB 20,000. Wei Guoquan's conduct did not constitute theft, and the court was requested to correctly apply the law and impose a punishment commensurate with the crime.

The defendant Wei Guoquan submitted a receipt from Zheng Wei to prove that he voluntarily paid RMB 20,000 to compensate the vehicle owner and driver, which Zheng Wei accepted.

The Xi'an Intermediate People's Court found through trial:

At approximately 6:00 a.m. on April 10, 2004, the defendant Wei Guoquan (a taxi driver) passed by Wenyi Road, Xi'an, on his way to work and noticed a white Lexus 400 sedan parked on the motor vehicle lane with all four windows down, headlights on, and no one inside. About an hour later, Wei Guoquan drove past the same section of road again and found the vehicle still parked in the same place. He then parked his taxi, surreptitiously entered the white Lexus, and, noticing the keys were still in the ignition and no one was interfering, drove the car away and concealed it in the parking lot of the 323 Hospital of the People's Liberation Army on Jianshe West Road, Xi'an. Subsequently, Wei Guoquan inspected the vehicle and found the owner's identification, business cards, mobile phone, leather shoes, golf clubs, and US$200. Wei Guoquan used the mobile phone and leather shoes, squandered the US dollars, and hid the golf clubs at his sister's home. To facilitate his use, he also had the vehicle repaired and changed its license plates. In January 2005, the victim discovered the stolen vehicle, and the public security organs arrested Wei Guoquan. The stolen vehicle and golf clubs and other items were returned to the victim. The appraisal determined the value of the white Lexus 400 sedan (license plate Shaan A-L5408) to be RMB 373,380. After the incident, Wei Guoquan voluntarily paid RMB 20,000 to compensate the vehicle owner and driver, which Zheng Wei accepted.

The issues in dispute in this case are: 1. Whether the vehicle involved is a "mislaid item"? 2. Whether Wei Guoquan's act of driving away the vehicle involved constitutes stealing by stealth? 3. Whether Wei Guoquan had the purpose of illegal possession with respect to the vehicle involved?

The Xi'an Intermediate People's Court held:

I. Regarding whether the vehicle involved is a "mislaid item".

A mislaid item is a concept in the crime of embezzlement under Article 270 of the Criminal Law of the PRC, and is a unique object of that crime. A mislaid item refers to property that should have been carried but was left behind due to forgetfulness. The owner of the property should subjectively realize that he/she has forgotten the property and has lost control over it. To determine whether the vehicle in this case is a mislaid item, we must first analyze the victim's subjective awareness. According to the facts of this case, the victim Zheng Wei drove home after drinking alcohol and parked the car on the road near his residence. Due to excessive drinking, he did not close the doors or windows and left the keys in the car, but he did not lose control over the car. Several hours later, Zheng Wei discovered the vehicle was stolen and immediately reported it to the public security authorities. The time from when Zheng Wei parked the car to when he discovered it stolen and reported it was very short, and he stated that the location where the vehicle was stolen was consistent with the location where the defendant Wei Guoquan confessed to stealing it. This sufficiently proves that Zheng Wei did not subjectively forget the vehicle. Second, Zheng Wei's intoxicated state merely weakened his control over the vehicle. If Wei Guoquan had not committed the theft, Zheng Wei could have fully regained control over the vehicle. In this case, from the time Zheng Wei parked the car by the roadside until it was stolen by Wei Guoquan, there was a period of two hours, during which the vehicle remained undisturbed. If Zheng Wei had sobered up during this time, he could naturally have regained control of the vehicle. However, when Zheng Wei did sober up, he discovered the vehicle was missing, and the actual loss of control occurred precisely because of Wei Guoquan's act of driving the car away and concealing it. Therefore, Wei Guoquan's theft was the fundamental reason for the victim's loss of control over the vehicle. Third, a mislaid item refers to property that should have been carried but was left behind due to forgetfulness. An automobile, as property, has special attributes. This special nature is reflected in the fact that the purchase and transfer of vehicles require registration and issuance of certificates through the vehicle administration authorities. If, disregarding the special material nature of motor vehicles and their status and function in people's lives, one were to classify them as mislaid items simply because the owner or user forgot to close the windows or doors or left the keys behind, such a conclusion would be contrary to common sense. Therefore, the defense counsel's argument on this point is untenable.

II. Regarding whether Wei Guoquan's act of driving away the vehicle involved constitutes stealing by stealth.

Stealing by stealth refers to an actor's conduct of illegally taking possession of property by means that the actor subjectively believes will not be discovered by the owner, custodian, or handler of the property. Such surreptitious means are relative to the owner, custodian, or handler of the property, and are based on the actor's subjective belief that the act will not be discovered; it is not necessary that others are actually unaware or cannot detect it. In this case, the abnormal condition of the vehicle involved — windows left open, doors unlocked, keys left in the ignition — not only created a convenient opportunity for the defendant Wei Guoquan to commit theft but also made the form of his surreptitious means different from that of typical theft crimes (such as breaking locks or smashing windows). However, this does not mean that Wei Guoquan's conduct was not surreptitious. As found through trial, Wei Guoquan entered the car only after discovering that it had been unattended for a long time, and drove it away and concealed it when he was sure he would not be detected. His conduct fully satisfies the objective elements of theft under criminal law, i.e., taking another's property by stealth. Therefore, this argument of the defense counsel lacks factual and legal basis, is untenable, and is not accepted.

III. Regarding whether Wei Guoquan had the purpose of illegal possession with respect to the vehicle involved.

It is established that during his use of the vehicle, the defendant Wei Guoquan changed the license plates, disguised the vehicle, had it repaired multiple times for his convenience, and possessed and used it for as long as nine months until he was arrested. Furthermore, Wei Guoquan squandered, used, or concealed the US dollars and personal items stored in the vehicle. His intent of illegal possession is evident. Therefore, the defense counsel's claim that Wei Guoquan did not have the intent of illegal possession when he drove away the vehicle involved is not supported. As for Wei Guoquan's own argument that he had intended to return the vehicle on several occasions, it is established that after stealing the vehicle, Wei Guoquan immediately discovered the owner's identification and contact telephone number, and his brother repeatedly urged him to return the vehicle, but Wei Guoquan ignored these and continued to possess and use it for a long time. Therefore, this defense is untenable.

IV. The defense counsel's argument that, after the incident, the defendant Wei Guoquan proactively compensated the victim for economic losses in the amount of RMB 20,000 is verified.

Wei Guoquan secretly stole another person's property, the amount being particularly huge, but he voluntarily compensated the victim for economic losses, and the stolen vehicle was recovered, resulting in no significant economic loss to the victim. Accordingly, a lighter punishment may be imposed at the court's discretion.

Based on the above, on June 11, 2005, the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment:

The defendant Wei Guoquan was convicted of theft and sentenced to 10 years' imprisonment, with a fine of RMB 10,000.

Wei Guoquan, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Shaanxi High People's Court on the ground that driving away the vehicle involved was merely an illegal appropriation of another's mislaid item and that he lacked subjective intent of illegal possession, and therefore his conduct did not constitute theft.

The Shaanxi High People's Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to hear the case. After reviewing the case files, it determined that the facts of the case were clear and decided not to hold a hearing. Upon trial, it confirmed the facts found by the first-instance court.

The Shaanxi High People's Court held:

Whether an item involved is a "mislaid item" should be judged in light of the specific circumstances of the case and with reference to the norms of daily social life. With respect to property, it can generally be classified into movable and immovable property based on whether it can be moved and whether moving it would impair its economic value. There is a type of movable property that is relatively special, such as motor vehicles and ships. Although they can be moved and their economic value is not affected by moving, these items are of significant value, and the owner must assert ownership by means of a certificate of title. For related transactions, ownership is transferred only after the registration of the transfer has been completed. Their real rights changes follow the rules for immovable property changes, making them distinct from ordinary movables. For ordinary movables, the external manifestation of becoming a mislaid item is that no one is near the item or no one claims dominion over it. However, for property such as motor vehicles, possession and control do not require a special declaration, nor is constant physical control a prerequisite. The driver leaving the vehicle does not mean a complete loss of control over the motor vehicle. On the other hand, from the perspective of daily social life, the relationship of dominion of the owner or possessor over a motor vehicle parked on the roadside is not affected even if the windows are left open, doors are unlocked, or keys are left in the ignition. Even if the external appearance of the motor vehicle is temporarily unattended, common sense dictates that it is not a forgotten item. Therefore, even though the windows and doors of the vehicle involved were left open and the keys were left in the ignition, it cannot be presumed to be a mislaid item.

The appellant Wei Guoquan committed the act of theft by stealth. Stealing by stealth refers to an actor's conduct of illegally taking possession of property by means that the actor subjectively believes will not be discovered by the owner, custodian, or handler of the property. Such surreptitious means are relative to the owner, custodian, or handler of the property; it is not required that others are actually unaware or cannot detect it. In this case, the abnormal condition of the vehicle involved — windows left open, doors unlocked, keys left in the ignition — not only created a convenient opportunity for Wei Guoquan to commit theft but also made the form of his surreptitious means different from that of typical theft crimes (such as breaking locks or smashing windows). However, this does not mean that Wei Guoquan's conduct was not surreptitious. Wei Guoquan entered the car only after discovering that it had been unattended for a long time, and drove it away and concealed it when he was sure he would not be detected, and he squandered or used the property inside the vehicle. Therefore, Wei Guoquan obtained the property by surreptitious illegal means. Subsequently, during his use of the vehicle, Wei Guoquan also changed its license plates. The change of real rights in motor vehicles follows the rules for changes in real rights in immovable property, and the relevant authorities' administration of motor vehicles also differs from that of ordinary movables. The license plate registration system further enhances the control of the owner or possessor over the vehicle. After a vehicle is lost, the owner can search for it through the relevant authorities based on the license plate number. Therefore, Wei Guoquan's act of changing the license plates was in fact a continuation of his surreptitious theft, thereby causing the owner to lose the possibility of locating the vehicle through its license plate and achieving his criminal purpose of theft.

The appellant Wei Guoquan had the purpose of illegal possession subjectively. After Wei Guoquan stole the vehicle, he immediately discovered the owner's identification and contact telephone number, and his brother repeatedly urged him to return it, but Wei Guoquan ignored these and continued to possess and use the vehicle, changed its license plates, had it repaired multiple times, and possessed and used it for as long as nine months until he was arrested. Furthermore, Wei Guoquan squandered, used, or concealed the US dollars and personal items stored in the vehicle. The above facts are sufficient to establish that Wei Guoquan subjectively had the purpose of illegal possession.

Based on the facts of this case, the appellant Wei Guoquan's conduct was not possession of a mislaid item, but rather secret theft of another's property with the purpose of illegal possession. His conduct constituted theft, and the amount stolen was particularly huge. After the incident, Wei Guoquan proactively compensated the victim for economic losses in the amount of RMB 20,000, which is verified. Given that Wei Guoquan voluntarily compensated the victim for economic losses and the stolen vehicle was recovered, resulting in no significant economic loss to the victim, a lighter punishment may be imposed at the court's discretion.

In summary, the appellant Wei Guoquan's appeal grounds — that "driving away the vehicle involved was merely an illegal appropriation of another's mislaid item and that he lacked subjective intent of illegal possession, and therefore his conduct did not constitute theft" — lack factual and legal basis and are untenable. The first-instance judgment had clear findings of fact, appropriate sentencing, and a lawful trial procedure, and should be affirmed.

Accordingly, on December 26, 2005, the Shaanxi High People's Court, pursuant to Article 189(1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC, ruled:

Appeal dismissed and judgment affirmed.
